output.brief: The drafted claim should not go out as written. The RFI platform's tamper-proof timestamps show the architect answered 62 of 64 queries within the contract period. The "41 late" figure comes from counting time while the queries sat in Callerby's own draft status. The three structural queries were answered in 2–5 days. The change orders are real, but CO-09, the only structural one, was issued on 6 November 2025. Our own tower crane had already left for Kestrel in October. Our progress report in November then described the crane's removal as a response to a design hold. The most likely main driver is therefore Callerby's own decision to move the crane and frame gang, and Halden already knows this. Sending a claim that blames Halden's architect risks credibility and the £1.9m. Settling by admitting everything is premature, though, because CO-09 may justify some real time. I'm moderately confident (about 65%). Next steps: hold the 1 December submission; have an independent analyst work out what the frame could have done without the crane, and how much time CO-09 really cost. Also check steel delivery. Don't discipline the superintendent for answering honestly. Don't scrap the incentive scheme until the link to the crane move is shown. Review how the crane was moved between projects.
